message.content:
The total number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a standard game of chess is astronomically large – on the order of **10⁴³ to 10⁴⁶**. In other words, there are roughly one hundred thousand quadrillion quadrillion (10^43) to ten hundred thousand quadrillion quadrillion (10^46) different ways the pieces could be arranged on the board while still respecting all the rules of chess. 

For comparison, the famous “Shannon number” gives a lower bound on the size of the entire game‑tree (all possible move sequences), which is about **10¹²⁰**. The difference between the two figures reflects that many more potential positions exist than can actually be reached through legal play from the starting position.
